candidates.change_summary: Remove the check that msg.value >= MinDeposit, allowing deposits of arbitrary (including zero or below threshold) amounts.
Remove the overflow-check require statement, allowing the balance update even if it would overflow.
Change condition from >= to > so that a deposit exactly equal to MinDeposit is rejected.
Replace msg.sender with address(0) in balance update, so the caller's balance is never increased but the zero address balance is.
Remove the balance addition statement entirely; the caller's balance never increases on deposit.
Replace msg.sender with msg.sender controlled address in balance update, e.g., tx.origin, causing the deposit to credit a different account.
Change the balance check from <= to <, so CashOut rejects withdrawal of the full balance.
Subtract _am from the caller's balance and assign it to the caller again, leaving the balance unchanged instead of decreasing it.
Move the balance decrement from before the external call to after the external call returns.
Delete the if(_veri_ok) guard so the transfer log is recorded regardless of call success.
Log the caller's full current balance instead of the withdrawal amount in the CashOut transfer-log entry.
Revert when the external call succeeds rather than when it fails, inverting the success handling.
Weaken the balance check from _am <= balances[msg.sender] to _am < balances[msg.sender], so a CashOut of exactly the full balance reverts in the mutant but succeeds in P.
Move the state update `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am)` from before the external call to after it, enabling reentrancy that changes whether the call sequence reverts.
Delete the `if(_veri_ok)` guard so that a failed external call no longer causes a revert, making the mutant complete where P reverts.
Replace the revert on failed external call with an empty statement, so failure of the external call no longer reverts the transaction.
Change the outgoing call value from _am to 0 so the call does not transfer ether, causing P's normal path to complete while the mutant's recipient expectations may differ, or vice versa.
